title: Karnataka: Congress names G S Patil Speaker nominee, Saleem Ahmed for Council chairperson - Deccan Herald
content:
Bengaluru: The Congress on Monday announced four-time Ron MLA G S Patil as its nominee for the post of Assembly Speaker. Patil hails from Lingayat community. In 2016, Patil was appointed Chairman of Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Limited. He was appointed as chairman of Mineral Development Corporation on Jan 26, 2024. The party has also announced that Virajpet MLA A S Ponnanna will be the party’s nominee for the post of deputy speaker. Ponnanna, who served as legal advisor for Siddaramaiah when he was CM, is a first-time MLA. In the Council, the Congress has announced three-time MLC Saleem Ahmed as its nominee for chairman’s post. Ahmed was also a ministerial aspirant. The party has nominated actor-politician Umashree as its candidate for the post of deputy chairperson. With the Congress having a comfortable majority in the Assembly and a slender majority in Council, all its nominees are expected to be elected. The session of the legislature starts on Aug 13. The election of Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman is expected on August 14. Cut-off box - Jayachandra is pro-tem Speaker
Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot appointed senior lawmaker T B Jayachandra as the pro-tem Speaker of the Assembly on Monday.
Jayachandra will oversee the election of the new Speaker. Congress has picked Ron MLA G S Patil as its Speaker nominee.

title: The BMW That Has Gold Wing Owners Rethinking Long-Distance Touring - Top Speed
content: For a long time, traditional full-dressers have set the standard for luxury long-distance touring on two wheels. Harley-Davidson and Indian lead the pack with luxury galore and top-spec components. And metric luxury tourer options like the Honda Gold Wing do one better by offering more sophisticated technology for a relatively affordable price tag. Now, though, there's a new threat to this segment: large-capacity versatile adventure tourers. Not only do these ADVs offer similar levels of riding comfort, convenience, and luxury features, but they also edge ahead with added off-roading finesse. Want a reliable used luxury ADV tourer? Then, we have a definitive and affordable winner that will make you want to ditch your Gold Wing. Traditional touring bikes (especially the full dresser options) have nailed the formula to offer the most comfortable, luxurious, and stress-free cross-country riding experience. But versatility isn't their strong suit. Life on endless paved roads is great until a bad stretch or tight spaces come into the picture. Enter ADV tourers. They make a better case by offering more than 90 percent of a full-dresser's experience in a much lighter and more versatile package. Manufacturers BMW, Ducati, and Triumph particularly deserve credit for this, as they offer a long-distance version of their versatile, flagship ADVs with a bigger fuel tank and more mile-munching-focused comfort and convenience features. They come with relatively smaller road-focused wheels, less suspension travel, and more luggage space. Their off-roading capabilities are reduced, but they are still a lot better than what a low-slung full-dresser would offer. While new 2026 models are already impressive, we have a gold mine of used touring-ready adventure bikes at our disposal, too. If we pick the right one with impressive reliability and after-sales support, then a luxury touring experience can be had for as much as half the price of a new full-dresser. Thankfully, we don't have to look far because the BMW R 1250 GS Adventure fits this bill perfectly. The prime example of this is a used R 1250 GS Adventure. The standard R 1250 GS is already a great all-rounder. But the Adventure model takes things further, becoming a formidable luxury touring bike alternative. The GSA has a much larger 7.9-gallon fuel tank and more suspension travel. It comes standard with heavy-duty engine and tank crash bars, auxiliary lights, wider footpegs, a larger windscreen, and stainless steel luggage mounts for aluminum panniers. Thus, the 1250 GSA offers nearly 90 percent of the experience with the added advantage of scaling over rocky terrain with ease. The huge fuel tank should translate to an easy 350+ mile range (claimed fuel economy rating is ~47 miles per gallon). Then, we have the prices. Currently, the last-gen R 1250 GS models (2020 to 2023) are being sold for as low as $16,500 on the used marketplaces. We even stumbled upon a used 2024 model for under $17,000, which is a pretty good deal. Oh, and while BMW has replaced the R 1250 GS with the new tech-loaded R 1300 GS, the predecessor still packs enough punch to stand tall in 2026. In fact, a used R 1250 GS actually offers more value than the R 1300 GS, if you are unfazed by the intimidating dimensions of the former. The R 1250 GSA packs a proven liquid-cooled 1,254 cc boxer twin engine with 136 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 105 pound-feet of torque at 6,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual and a final shaft drive system. All the low-end oomph helps with its relaxed yet sprinty highway touring capabilities. The BMW badge might persuade you into thinking the GS is an expensive bike to maintain. That, however, is not the case because long service intervals help keep the GS up and about for longer. Upholding its globe-trotting ability is its durable build quality all around. BMW specifies an oil change every 6,000 miles or once a year, whichever comes first. The valve clearance checks are reserved for every 12,000 miles. Furthermore, the shaft drive eliminates the need to replace sprockets and tighten and lube a chain every few hundred miles. The shaft drive does need an inspection every 12,500 miles and a preventive replacement at 60,000 miles. This could become an expensive affair, but thankfully, BMW covers the shaft replacement for the lifetime of the vehicle at no cost to the owner. This benefit wasn't extended to the new R 1300 GS, making the 1250 GS more desirable on the ownership front. The R 1250 GSA is underpinned by a two-section frame consisting of the main frame and a bolt-on rear frame, with the mill being a stressed member here. The frame sits on a unique suspension setup: BMW's 37 mm Telelever setup with a central spring strut and BMW's Paralever assembly with a spring strut attached to a cast aluminum single-sided swing arm. The Telelever front setup is famed for offering a high level of anti-dive under hard braking and also elevates confidence when going fast or over rough terrain. The GSA electronic suspension control (optional when new) further helps with automatic damping and load compensation based on riding modes. This electronic control helps this nearly 600-pound tall-riding ADV behave as a stable highway runner, a commendable off-roader, and even a nimble mountain-road companion. As for the cockpit, there's a crisp TFT with smartphone connectivity. It enables access to a slew of standard safety, assistive, and convenience features, including Dynamic Traction Control, lean-sensitive ABS, Hill Start Control, and three ride modes (Eco, Rain, and Road). The optional suite is also solid, with the aforementioned Dynamic Electronic Suspension Adjustment with automatic load leveling, Riding Mode Pro with additional modes (Dynamic, Dynamic Pro, Enduro, and Enduro Pro), Automated Hill Start Control Pro, Dynamic Brake Assist, and Engine Brake Control. The best part about used motorcycles is that all of these optional features can be bundled for much less than the original price. Most used R 1250 GS specimens often come stacked with all optional features. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. The father of a Rajshahi University student who was pulled from an ambulance and beaten during the July 27 campus violence filed a case with a Rajshahi court today against nine people, including Rucsu General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar and Assistant General Secretary Salman Sabbir. Md Asad Uz Zaman filed the complaint with the Motihar Cognisance Court, accusing the nine and 17 to 18 unidentified others of attempting to murder his son, Md Mahmudul Hasan Mahin, a student of the university's Sanskrit department under the 2021-22 academic session. The other named accused are Nazmus Sakib, Mehedi Sanjib, Fahim Reza, Arifur Islam, Ahsan Ulla Faihan, Sifat Ar Saleh and Nurul Islam Shaheed. The complaint was filed under several sections of the Penal Code. According to the complaint, the accused, armed with knives, iron rods, belts and bamboo sticks, chased Mahin and surrounded him in and outside the university's central library between 12:30pm and 1:00pm on July 27. It alleged that Ammar hit Mahin on the head and forehead with an iron rod, while Sabbir also hit him on the head, injuring his left eye. The other accused also allegedly assaulted him. The complaint further alleged that four of the accused pinned Mahin to the ground, pressed down on his chest and throat, and tried to suffocate him. It also alleged that when teachers, students and others tried to take him to hospital in an ambulance, the accused pulled him out of the vehicle and assaulted him again. Mahin was later admitted to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital. His father said he learned about the incident through Facebook around 5:30pm on the day of the violence. He later went to the hospital and found his son undergoing treatment. He also alleged that the officer-in-charge of Motihar Police Station refused to register a case when he approached the police on July 28 and advised him to seek legal remedy through the court. Advocate Hazrat Ali, representing the accused, said the court did not pass any immediate order taking cognisance of the complaint and instead referred it to the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) for inquiry. He claimed that Mahin's father had filed the complaint "out of emotion". The violence on July 27 began after a dispute at the university's proctor's office, where the Rucsu GS and other leaders accused another student, Anas, of having links to the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League. Anas and several others were later accused of attacking the Rucsu office. Rucsu leaders and activists, joined by members of Islami Chhatra Shibir, later entered the central library's reading room and assaulted three students, according to witnesses and videos reviewed by this newspaper. Videos also showed Mahin being pulled from an ambulance and beaten as teachers attempted to send him to hospital. title: GS Caltex Hosts 'Family Day' with Vice Chairman Huh Sae-hong - Seoul Economic Daily

Experiencing GS Caltex Yeosu Plant Using MR and VR
"Hope You Grow Into the Energy of Future Society" GS Caltex hosted a "Family Day" inviting the families of its employees to experience digital technology firsthand. GS Caltex said on the 3rd that it held the event under the theme "Energy to the Future" at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on the 31st of last month. Vice Chairman Huh Sae-hong attended the event and expressed his gratitude. Employees' families spent time understanding the value chain of the energy business through game content developed directly by the GS Caltex DAX (Digital & AI Transformation) Center. They also viewed panoramic scenes of the GS Caltex Yeosu plant using mixed reality (MR) and virtual reality (VR), and experienced MR- and VR-based safety training content currently in use at actual sites. In addition, they enjoyed a variety of programs, including hands-on activities using digital technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) Go and Omok, as well as making eco-bags and keyrings and taking family photos. "I hope today's experience remains a pleasant memory and leads to a good opportunity for pursuing dreams going forward," Huh said. title: Why Did Banking Stocks GS, JPM, BAC Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS), JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), and Bank of America Corp. (BAC) surged to annual highs after the banks posted stellar second-quarter earnings results that beat market expectations. GS stock led the climb among banking stocks, surging more than 9% after its record Q2 results triggered a buy-in. JPM stock rose 2.5% after its results surged past Wall Street expectations, while BAC stock also soared nearly 2% to a record high. GS stock climbed to a record high of $1,143.84 on Tuesday after the company reported record Q2 results that tore past analysts’ expectations. Goldman Sachs posted quarterly revenue of $20.98 billion, significantly higher than Wall Street's $16.4 billion estimate, according to Koyfin data. The investment bank also reported earnings of $15.91 per share, ahead of the $14.40 consensus estimate, while net income reached a record $6.32 billion for the quarter. The strong results were fueled by robust performance in investment banking, equities trading, and asset management, as companies continued to tap capital markets and pursue AI-related financing and strategic deals. "There's a lot of capital out there," CEO David Solomon said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday. "I'm not concerned about the ability for the capital to be available for things that make sense." GS stock has surged nearly 25% so far this year. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing. JPM stock climbed to a 52-week high of $344.73 on Tuesday, driven by strong Q2 results that boosted investor interest in the company. The bank posted revenue of $57.35 billion versus a consensus estimate of $51.3 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) came in at $7.70 per share versus an expectation of $ 5.80 per share, based on Fiscal.ai data. JPMorgan delivered its strongest trading quarter on record, with trading revenue jumping 35% year over year to $12.1 billion. CEO Jamie Dimon said every business segment achieved record results, noting that market conditions remain favorable for sustained activity. Investment banking fees climbed 30% from a year earlier to $3.3 billion, marking their highest level since 2021, while net interest income rose 10% year over year to $25.6 billion. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs raised the price target on the bank to $418 from $411 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after its Q2 earnings beat, as per TheFly. JPM stock has gained more than 5% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over 24 hours. BAC stock also climbed to a record high of $61.21 on Tuesday, driven by Q2 results that demonstrated a strong investment banking pipeline amid growing AI demand. The bank reported revenue of $31.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $30.7 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.21, beating expectations of $1.13 EPS. Investment banking revenue climbed 50% year-over-year, with sales and trading revenue rising 30%. A surge of more than 70% in equities trading was the standout performer, contributing to one of the bank's best quarters in recent years. "We still have very strong pipelines in investment banking. The IPOs and deals are still getting done, and very strong interest in doing transactions,” CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC in an interview. "The AI buildout still has a lot of debt funding and other funding required, so it's a very good environment." Meanwhile, Jefferies raised the price target on Bank of America to $75 from $70 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after a "strong quarter," as per TheFly. BAC stock has gained more than 8% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. (ORCL) and Hertz Global Holdings (HTZ), all sank to fresh 52-week lows on Tuesday on growing concerns over profitability, financing needs and balance-sheet pressure across industries. Lucid stock crashed 16% during the trading session, and Oracle fell 2%. Hertz Global regained losses and ended Tuesday 0.5% higher. Lucid stock faced one of the most turbulent trading sessions in its history on Tuesday, plummeting to an intraday record low of $2.37 after restructuring speculation triggered a dramatic sell-off in the luxury electric vehicle maker’s shares. The steep decline followed reports that restructuring adviser AlixPartners was reviewing options for the company, including possibilities that investors interpreted as potential bankruptcy or a private-market transaction. Lucid moved quickly to deny the claims, saying the bankruptcy-related speculation was “completely false.” The company said AlixPartners was assisting with operational improvements, including cost management, manufacturing efficiency and supply-chain efforts rather than preparing for insolvency proceedings. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock jumped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bearish’ territory the previous day. Oracle stock fell to a one-year low of $127.83 as investors questioned the financial burden of its aggressive expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company’s stock has declined 33% over the past month as concerns about spending, financing needs, and customer concentration have overshadowed optimism about its large cloud business. Oracle has a huge backlog of cloud orders, but the company is taking on more debt to build the data centers needed to complete those contracts. A major factor weighing on Oracle has been a downgrade from S&P Global, which lowered the company’s credit rating to BBB-, only one level above non-investment-grade status. The agency highlighted concerns about Oracle’s reliance on large customers, including OpenAI, which represents a large portion of its remaining performance obligations. Retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘extremely bullish’ territory. Hertz Global stock fell to a six-year low of $1.75 as investors reacted to falling used-vehicle prices, heavy debt obligations and weakening financial conditions. The company also reported higher fleet depreciation costs, adding pressure to its recovery efforts. Retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘bullish’ territory. According to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 3.5% year-on-year, below market expectations. Meanwhile, core inflation came in at 2.6%, with prices declining 0.4% from the previous month, the largest monthly drop since May 2020. Lower energy costs drove the decline in headline inflation, with the energy index falling 5.7% in June. The softer inflation figures lowered expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve. According to the CME's FedWatch tool, the probability of a rate hike at the July meeting fell to 15.5%, down from 41.7% a day earlier. Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) rebounded after a six-session losing streak on Tuesday as CEO Peter Beck highlighted the company as one of the few proven commercial launch providers, calling SpaceX a “friendly rival” and noting that Rocket Lab emerged from a field of more than 100 failed challengers. RKLB stock jumped nearly 3% on Tuesday, with shares also up nearly 2% overnight. In a recent BBC interview, Beck said commercial launch remains exceptionally difficult despite billions of dollars in investment. “Despite billions of dollars and over 100 companies trying, there has actually only been two companies to pop out the other end,” with a regular and reliable launch service, he said, in a discussion that also touched on Rocket Lab’s rivalry with SpaceX. “Launch and a commercial company doing launch still remains extremely rare,” Beck added. Beck called SpaceX a “friendly rival” and said space companies often compete for one contract before working together on another: “You can be competing tooth and tail for a particular contract” and later team up to deliver it, he said. Rocket Lab can also benefit when rivals win as it supplies components such as reaction wheels, star trackers and solar panels.” “We can go head to head with a traditional space prime and then lose,” Beck said. “And then the next day, there’s a purchase order.” Beck called Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company spanning satellites, launch and services from orbit: “We build satellites, we launch them on our rockets and we provide services from space,” he said. Pointing to SpaceX’s Falcon 9 and Starlink model, Beck added: “They’re able to do all those things. And we’re able to do those too.” William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma recently named Rocket Lab and Blue Origin among the strongest challengers to SpaceX, though he said SpaceX still holds more than 90% of the launch market. Rocket Lab is advancing its competitive vertical integration strategy through its $8 billion acquisition of Iridium Communications, which would add a global network, spectrum, and recurring satellite service revenue. The company recently completed a full-duration burn of its Archimedes Vacuum engine, an important step toward the first flight of its reusable Neutron rocket. Rocket Lab said it was “critical preparation for Neutron’s first flight.” Beck has told Stocktwits earlier that Rocket Lab is “pushing very hard” to launch Neutron by the fourth quarter of 2026, while cautioning that the challenge is not merely reaching orbit but proving the rocket can return and be reused. “If we just had to go up, it’s super easy, we’d be in orbit by now,” he previously said. Rocket Lab also completed the U.S. Space Force’s Victus Haze mission, launching 16 hours and 42 minutes after receiving notice and completing spacecraft commissioning and proximity operations ahead of schedule. The company supplied the launch vehicle, spacecraft and orbital operations under one contract, offering a practical demonstration of the integrated model Beck outlined in the interview. Shares of top software companies, including ServiceNow and Salesforce, fell on Tuesday after IBM reported preliminary quarterly results showing acute weakness in its software business and said clients were shifting spending to AI servers faster than anticipated. ServiceNow stock declined 5.8%, while Adobe and Salesforce’s shares dropped 4.3% and 2.1%, respectively. Software heavyweight Microsoft closed 1.6% lower as well. The group edged higher in overnight trading, led by Microsoft, which rose 0.4%. "While we anticipated some supply-chain related impact in our expectations, we did not anticipate ​the magnitude of the capex reprioritization," Krishna said, adding that the company “faltered” and "numerous large deals" had failed to close as expected. IBM said the weakness was largely in its mainframe business, which sells high-end enterprise computers and related software that power mission-critical workloads, including processing massive volumes of transactions for banks, governments, airlines, and retailers. Could be an inflection point if positive.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. General Fusion Group Ltd. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes. title: Is BMW Working on an M 1300 GS? All Signs Point to Yes - inkl
content:
BMW's R 1300 GS is the brand's best-selling motorcycle, and for good reason; it's bloody amazing. It has been the most popular BMW for years, so how could the Bavarian brand further expand its dominance? Well, it could make an M version. As reported by SpeedWeek, it looks like BMW is making an M 1300 GS, which would become the brand's flagship off-road motorcycle. If this comes as a surprise to you, you're not alone. Historically, the 'M' badge has been reserved for BMW's sportiest road-focused vehicles, with 'M' referring to motorsport. The exact shape an M 1300 GS would take is still unknown, but thanks to some spy shots, we have a few clues. In the spy shots, the bikes are under tarpaulins while being transported, but it looks like they're in the later stages of development. What's clear from the photos is that the M badge and features that come with it don't intend to turn the 1300 GS into a road-going phenom, but rather expand on its already impressive off-road capabilities. The bikes have 21-inch front wheels and 18-inch rear wheels, which are fitted with Metzeler Karoo tires, which tell you all you need to know about the terrain this model is intended to perform on. It also looks like there's longer suspension and a redesigned support for the swingarm. The dead giveaway for this bike is the blue 'M' calipers, which should bring more stopping power than the bike's standard BMW-branded, although Brembo-manufactured, calipers. As for the powerplant, it appears as though the 1,300 cc water-cooled boxer remains unchanged, barring an 'M' insignia on the cylinder head covers. That said, with 145 hp and a bonkers 110 lb-ft of torque on tap, I don't think anyone will lose sleep over power gains for off-road use. Cosmetically, it's unclear from the pictures how far BMW will go in terms of an M makeover. Price too remains a mystery, but a BMW M 1000 RR is around $15,000 more than the standard model, whereas an M 1000 R is around $5,500 more, so I'd say it wouldn't be unreasonable to think an M 1300 GS could be $10,000 to 15,000 more than a standard R 1300 GS. title: At $11,799, Could This 1978 Mazda RX-7 GS Make You Go Hmmm? - Jalopnik
content: With no new rotary-powered cars currently on offer, people wanting to get in on the Dorito-shaped piston scene need to look to used cars like today's Nice Price or No Dice RX-7. Considering it's now a classic, let's decide if this Wankel is worth our time. In America, bigger is almost always better. We have bigger dinner plates than do most of the rest of the world. We also have bigger refrigerators to hold all that food needed to fill those bigger plates. That necessitates a larger kitchen to house the big fridge, demanding a bigger house around that, and likely a comparatively large driveway leading to that big-ass house. That super-sizing could make any normal-sized car or truck parked on the property seem dinky by comparison. In such a case, the mega-big six-door, lifted, and wide-tired 2006 Ford F350 we looked at last Friday would be the perfect accompaniment to any such oversized McMansion. Unfortunately for its builder/seller, a $55,000 asking price proved too large for most of our tastes. That was obvious in the comments and the extremely overwhelming 90% 'No Dice' loss the fancy Ford suffered in the vote. For the longest time, the Ford Motor Company maintained a relationship with Japan's Mazda Motors. Ford sold some massaged Mazdas as Mercury models, and shared its popular Explorer—albeit only in two-door form—with their Asian partners. At no time, however, did Ford ever sell any of Mazda's Wankel-engined products as its own. In fact, aside from NSU and a dalliance by Citroën that actually drove the company to bankruptcy, Mazda has pretty much gone it alone in cheerleading the rotary engine. Perhaps the most famous and beloved model to carry the triangle piston torch is the RX-7, and today we're looking at a fairly unmolested 120,000-mile 1978 GS edition to see what all the fuss is about. This Spark Yellow over beige vinyl RX-7 hails from the model's first year on the market. It entered the U.S. market replacing the Cosmo, becoming Mazda's sole rotary offering in North America over three ensuing models and its RX-8 replacement. According to the seller, they have owned the car for 13 years, and it came with a fresh build of its 12A two-rotor motor at that time. That 1146cc Wankel put out a laudable 100 horsepower when new. Per the ad, this one has a Racing Beat header and exhaust, so perhaps it makes a couple more ponies. Everything looks stock under the sloping hood, although a missing belt on what looks to be an air-injection pump does raise questions. Backing the engine up is a five-speed manual transmission driving the solid rear axle. Braking is by discs in the front and drums in the rear, masked by handsome factory four-spoke alloy wheels. Those wheels look to be in great condition, as does the bodywork atop them. Age has taken its toll on the matte black paint on the windscreen pillars and license plate lamp housings, but aside from those minor issues, it's difficult to tell the car from new. Unfortunately, the ad doesn't say whether it drives as well as it looks. One thing that can be gleaned from the pictures in the ad is that the car's interior has not staved off Father Time as well as the exterior has. 1970s plastics don't have the same mojo as modern ones do, a fact made obvious by the cracked dashboard, broken door lever surrounds, and split seam in the driver's seat. Additionally, there are faded window cranks, worn silver paint on the dash separator, and a tear in the passenger-side door cover. Do any of those issues kill this Mazda's appeal? Probably not. Taken as a whole, though, the interior's flaws should offer some wiggle room in negotiating a deal on the car. Replacement parts for these cars are going to be next to impossible to obtain, after all, so its current condition is likely going to have to be lived with by its next owner. One final note about the interior is the stereo, as it's in stereo, with a more modern unit having been placed in the dash under the factory-installed one. That's kind of weird. In the plus column, this is a GS model and so comes with a sunroof. That's a glass panel, which the seller claims is a fairly rare inclusion. Aside from the stereo and the exhaust, this SA RX-7 appears to be completely stock and in very decent condition. It also carries a clean title and will come with some original literature and a few maintenance receipts. That's everything you might expect from a well-cared-for car. To take possession of this RX-7, there is the small matter of the $11,799 the seller is asking for it. That, they warn, is the only deal they are willing to entertain, as trades are off the table. Additionally, they only want to deal with serious inquiries, so low-ballers and shenanigan-eers need not apply. What do you think about this tidy if flawed RX-7 when its $11,799 asking price is taken into account? Does that seem fair for the car as it's presented in its ad? Or do the interior foibles demand a lower asking price? Chicago, Illinois, Craigslist, or go here if the ad disappears. Help me out with Nice Price or No Dice. title: 20 MLAs inducted into Karnataka cabinet; GS Patil to be Speaker - The Tribune
content: In a deft move, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday inducted 20 ministers in the first expansion of his cabinet since taking charge of the top post. Many of the faces are new with a mix of caste and regional arithmetics essential to the southern state. History The expansion strengthens the Shivakumar cabinet that took charge of the state back in June. The influential Vokkaliga leader had replaced Siddaramaiah in a leadership change that had long been the subject of a power tussle in Karnataka. With the latest round of expansion, the cabinet strength rises from 14 to 34. The new leaders include P M Narendraswamy (Malavalli), Shivaraj Tangadagi (Kanakagiri), Rudrappa Lamani (Haveri), K S Basavanthappa (Mayakonda), B Nagendra (Ballari rural), T Raghumoourthy (Challakere), B Z Zameer Ahmed Khan (Chamarajpet), Rizwan Arshad (Shivajinagar), Santosh Lad (Kalaghatagi), Madhu Bangarappa (Soraba), among others. G S Patil has been chosen as the new speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, while A S Ponnanna will serve as the deputy speaker. The expansion marks the comeback of former Scheduled Tribes welfare minister B Nagendra. A former BJP leader, who had moved to the Congress in 2018, Nagendra had resigned from the cabinet in 2024 over charges linked to the Valmiki Development Corporation scam. Besides, two minority faces are also part of the expansion—B Z Zameer Ahmed Khan and Rizwan Arshad. Children of three former chief ministers are now part of Shivakumar’s Cabinet. They are Yathindra Siddaramaiah (already a minister), Kumar Bangarappa (son of S Bangarappa) and Ajay Singh (son of N Dharam Singh). Incidentally, six of these 20 new ministers were part of the previous government led by Siddaramaiah. Gayathri Shanthegowda, whom the Supreme Court’s recent verdict declared elected from the Chikkamagaluru Local Authorities’ Constituency, will be the lone woman member in the Cabinet. Her election followed the court setting aside BJP’s M K Pranesh’s election to the legislative council in December 2021. Former deputy chief minister Laxman Savadi and Shivalinge Gowda, who joined the Congress from the BJP and JD(S), respectively, ahead of the 2023 assembly polls, are also becoming ministers this time. This much-awaited cabinet expansion aims to maintain social and regional representation, including adequate representation for AHINDA communities, women and younger legislators. The leadership is also seeking to strike a balance between legislators considered close to Shivakumar and those aligned with Siddaramaiah. AHINDA  politics refers to a powerful social and electoral coalition in Karnataka representing ‘Alpasankhyataru’ (minorities), ‘Hindulidavaru’ (backward classes), and ‘Dalitaru’ (dalits). The expansion was expected to take place earlier but was delayed as the Congress leadership worked to strike a balance between experienced leaders and first-time ministers while ensuring equitable representation across Karnataka’s regions and communities. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Shivakumar urged disappointed legislators to remain patient, saying it was “not possible to accommodate everyone” in the ministry. Recalling his own  political journey, he said he too had once missed out on a cabinet berth before eventually becoming a minister. “Similarly, we will ensure that everyone gets an opportunity in the future,” he said. His remarks came after Congress MLA Yashwantrayagouda V Patil resigned after missing out on a cabinet berth, while Belur MLA Gopalakrishna is expected to follow suit, according to sources. More than 15 disgruntled legislators also held a closed-door meeting at senior leader P V Jayachandra’s residence in Bengaluru to discuss their next course of action. Sources said senior leaders, including H K Patil and Dinesh Gundu Rao, attended the meeting. Visitors also experienced mixed-reality and virtual-reality content featuring the company’s Yeosu refinery, including safety training programs used by employees at the site. Other activities included AI-powered board games, robot soccer, motion-sensing sports, eco-bag and key ring making, and family photo sessions. GS Caltex Vice Chair Hur Sae-hong greeted employees’ families and thanked them for their support. “I hope Family Day helped our employees’ families better understand GS Caltex and their parents’ workplace, while taking pride in what they do,” Hur said. “I also hope the experience becomes a cherished memory and inspires the children to pursue their dreams and become the energy our future society needs.” Highest-level heat wave warning issued for Greater Seoul area Seoul and parts of Gyeonggi Province came under the capital region’s first Heat Wave Emergency Warning on Monday, as record-breaking heat in southeastern South Korea spread westward. title: How Michael McDonald's 1982 Yacht Rock Hit Inspired Warren G's Iconic 'Regulate' in Hip-Hop - Yahoo News UK
content: In 1982, yacht rock legend Michael McDonald released his debut solo single, "I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near)." Twelve years later, Warren G and Nate Dogg sampled the track for their own iconic hit, "Regulate," immortalizing the foundational melody, bridging the gap between musical genres, and launching one of the greatest commercial crossovers of all time. 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade's Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 Written by McDonald and Ed Sanford, "I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near)" officially marked the end of the former's Doobie Brothers era. It features background vocals from his sisterMaureen and actually borrows from another song itself: Chuck Jackson's 1962song of the same name. "As a jumping-off point, [McDonald and Sanford] borrowed the refrain melody and phrase from a 1962 song called "I Keep Forgettin'" by R&B legend Chuck Jackson," American Songwriter explained. "That original song was written by the iconic songwriting duo of Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, and the pair received songwriting credit on McDonald's song because of its debt to the earlier track." In McDonald's version, he sings of a jilted lover who forgets he and his significant other aren't together any longer: "I keep forgettin' we're not in love anymore / I keep forgettin' things will never be the same again," he sings. It actually became the solo artist's biggest song, peaking at No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100, following the Jackson original's climb to No. 55. But the hip-hop original McDonald inspired more than a decade later did even better. "In 1994, 'I Keep Forgettin' (Every Time You're Near),' which itself owed much to a song from many years earlier, was able to pay it forward," AS shares. "The hip-hop song 'Regulate' by Warren G featuring Nate Dogg soared to No. 2 on the pop charts, and it featured a foundational sample of McDonald's solo classic." In the '90s, Warren G and the late Nate Dogg were on top of their game, rising from local West Coast underground associates to mainstream international stars, fueled by the monumental success of their smash rap anthem, "Regulate." Speaking to Billboard in 2014, Warren G explains that he pulled from McDonald's classic because he thought it was "incredible." "I'm a fan. I'm still a fan," he said. "I really love his work, man. I think he's one of the greatest of all time. His voice is incredible. … Plus, it's a record my stepmom and my pops used to play. It brought back feelings for me of living with my parents, when we lived in North Long Beach. They used to jam with some good music, man." Featured on the Above the Rimsoundtrack in March 1994, the track, which also samples dialogue from the 1988 cult western Young Guns, was then released as a single on Warren G's solo debut album, Regulate… G Funk Era, in June 1994 via Def Jam Recordings and Violator Records. The track helped boost the record to the No. 2 spot on the Billboard 200 and earned a Grammy nomination in 1995 for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. Widely considered one of the defining songs of G-funk, or gangsta funk, "Regulate" sold more than a million copies and was certified platinumin August 1994 by the RIAA. It has since earned triple platinum honors. Perhaps even better, though, McDonald has said publicly that he loves the rap song. "There's great stuff that's taken the genre to a new level over the years, and 'Regulate' was one of those tracks that was kind of a landmark," McDonald told Billboard in 2014. Today, both tracks—the soft rock staple and the hip-hop essential—are the source of a meme about fans who have reached a certain point when they freeze at the opening keyboard notes of both songs, unsure if they're about to hear smooth '80s yacht rock or stellar '90s G-funk. As fans online often phrase it, "Michael McDonald walked so Warren G could Regulate." Together, they represent one of popular music's most successful examples of a song transcending generations, genres, platforms--and even meme culture. title: BMW M 1300 GS: what the spy shots reveal - motorcycles.news
content:
At BMW, the letter M has stood for motorsport since the 1980s. For a long time the badge was reserved for the cars; today three motorcycles carry it as well: the M 1000 RR from 36,300 euros, the M 1000 R from 23,290 euros and the M 1000 XR from 26,590 euros. That a fourth model would follow became apparent early on. Back in 2019, BMW secured the naming rights to the designation M 1300 GS. In spring 2022, the names R 1300 GS, R 1400 GS and M 1300 GS additionally appeared prematurely on a BMW service page and disappeared again shortly afterwards. There was never an official confirmation. Now new photographs deliver the clearest indication yet that development is entering the home straight. The photos show an almost fully developed prototype being transported under a tarpaulin. Photographer Bernhard M. Höhne did not manage to catch any running test bikes, meaning camouflaged pre-production machines. Even so, a fair amount can be read from them. One important clue is the level of maturity: in early development stages, prototypes from every manufacturer usually lack details such as lettering. Here, exactly those details are present. The M logo sits on the wheel, and the M colours that have been established for years appear on the left-hand valve cover. So it should not be all that long until an unveiling. The scene was captured at the end of July 2026, and it came as a double act. Right next to the M 1300 GS stood a second covered motorcycle, which according to media reports is the revised R 1300 GS. Comparing the two machines is what really makes the differences visible. The larger front wheel is the clearest sign that the M 1300 GS is meant to be far more capable off-road than any other boxer GS. A 21-inch wheel is used at the front and an 18-inch item at the rear, both with spokes. This combination is familiar from the air- and oil-cooled R 12 G/S. It helps a motorcycle roll over roots, rocks and deep ruts more easily, but costs a little agility on tarmac. Fittingly, the prototype on show wore knobbly Metzeler Karoo tyres. Hidden beneath the cover are longer suspension travel plus a sturdier, reworked support for the shaft-drive swingarm, meaning the assembly that takes the drive to the rear wheel. That makes the concept fundamentally different from the HP version of the previous R 1250 GS. That bike was essentially a visually upgraded equipment variant. With the M 1300 GS, by contrast, everything points to a thorough rebuild. Also clearly visible are the stronger M brakes with their characteristic blue calipers. Little appears to change on the drivetrain side. The 1300 cc liquid-cooled boxer of the R 1300 GS produces 145 hp (107 kW) at 7,750 rpm and delivers 149 Nm (110 lb-ft) at 6,500 rpm. The engineers could probably squeeze out a few more horsepower, although that would not be strictly necessary. The decisive lever lies elsewhere: the M 1300 GS is set to be noticeably lighter than the base model. Less mass improves the power-to-weight ratio without any changes to the engine. That is precisely what benefits a motorcycle most in demanding terrain. BMW is apparently attacking the weight from several angles. Part of it is expected to come from design measures, another part from premium materials. Titanium is said to be used in the exhaust system, among other places. Unlike the R 1300 GS Adventure, the M version is likely to use the standard tank of the regular R 1300 GS. That not only saves weight, it also distributes the remaining mass more favourably. How deep the visual changes go remains open. A revised seat unit is considered certain, a new subframe highly likely. Dropping the radar units at the front and rear would not be surprising either, because that step would also save weight. On the current models, the radar technology controls the adaptive cruise control and the blind-spot warning, but it offers little benefit off-road. The bottom line is that the M 1300 GS is moving away from the classic adventure tourer and towards a sports machine intended to show what a GS is capable of today. No price is known, but the existing M models provide a reference point. In Europe, the M 1000 XR and M 1000 R without extras sit on average 6,000 to 8,000 euros above the next cheapest version. On the US market the gap is bigger. There, the two M models are separated from the next cheapest variant by roughly 8,000 to 12,000 US dollars. A similar gap to the base model is to be expected for the M 1300 GS. Lower production numbers combined with a higher margin for the manufacturer fit that picture. The M 1300 GS should therefore sit at the top of the boxer range in terms of both capability and price. There is no official date. A launch before the 2027 season is nevertheless considered likely. Before that, a gentle revision of the best-selling R 1300 GS is still due, possibly as early as the beginning of autumn. One clue comes from BMW’s official model year 2027 list, published on 2 July 2026 and valid from August 2026. The R 1300 GS and the R 1300 GS Adventure are missing from it entirely, as are the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS. From the enduro corner, only the retro variant R 12 G/S is listed, and in the new colour Frozen Brooklyn Grey metallic at that. Models missing from such a list are usually an indication that something new is coming. According to media reports, the revised R 1300 GS is expected to go into production straight after the factory holidays in September, among other finishes in a light yellow that shimmered through the cover on the spy shot. For the 2027 model year, a three-way split of the boxer GS is emerging. Alongside the revised R 1300 GS and the R 1300 GS Adventure, the M 1300 GS is set to join as the new flagship. The three models would take on different jobs. The R 1300 GS remains the all-rounder, the Adventure with its large tank the long-distance specialist, and the M 1300 GS occupies the sporty off-road corner. BMW is thereby responding to a trend visible across the whole class: adventure bikes are increasingly being fanned out into different directions instead of covering everything with a single model. This plan has not been confirmed so far, but the evidence from spy shots and model lists points clearly in that direction. No. BMW has still not officially announced the model. What is documented are the naming rights secured in 2019, the appearance of the designation on a BMW service page in 2022 and the current images of a far-developed prototype. There is no official figure. The boxer engine of the R 1300 GS produces 145 hp (107 kW) and 149 Nm (110 lb-ft) and is expected to stay largely unchanged. A slight increase in power would be possible, but is not considered essential. The biggest difference lies in the chassis: a 21-inch front wheel, an 18-inch rear wheel, longer suspension travel and a reinforced support for the shaft-drive swingarm. Added to that are M brakes with blue calipers, the smaller standard tank and lightweight construction with titanium parts. The revision is expected in early autumn 2026. Since the R 1300 GS is missing from the model year list valid from August 2026, production should start straight after the factory holidays in September. The M has stood for motorsport since the 1980s and marks the sportiest models in the range. Among the motorcycles, it has so far been carried by the M 1000 RR, the M 1000 R and the M 1000 XR. ➜ This article is part of our comprehensive overview: New Motorcycles 2026: All Models, Releases, and Highlights at a Glance. title: The 'Slower' Sedan Now Worth Double a Used M5 - HotCars
content: Rahul Kapoor has been chasing cars on track, on the road, and occasionally on foot since 2014. His work has appeared in autoX, Motown India, and The Financial Express, covering everything from the latest EV tech to 1960s endurance racers. He’s not just a writer; he’s a photographer, videographer, and someone who’s actually lived inside the industry’s moving parts; attending launches, test-driving on race circuits, and talking shop with engineers, designers, and team principals. That mix of access and curiosity means his readers don’t just get the news; they get the story behind the story. There is a used sedan trading hands right now that lost every magazine comparison test it ever entered. It gave up horsepower, torque, and lap times to the German icon it was built to fight, and reviewers politely filed it away as a noble also-ran. Yet today, clean examples of this sports sedan are hammering for double — sometimes nearly triple — what that German benchmark brings at auction. Buyers are not paying for nostalgia or a badge. They are paying for something the spec sheets never measured, and the answer to this paradox sits in the engine bay. The numbers coming out of the auction world make no sense until you understand what is driving them. The highest price recorded on Cars and Bids for this sedan is $70,000 for a 2020 model, and early 2016 examples are not far behind, with three selling for $64,501 and others trading at $56,000 and $60,000. These are results for a car that struggled to find buyers when it was new. Its old rival is heading in the opposite direction. The same auction platform shows F10-generation BMW M5 prices sitting consistently in the $24,000 to $35,000 range, with very few examples creeping over $40,000. Even an M5 with the Competition Package hammered for just $46,000 — a striking result for the car that dominated its era. Here is what makes the inversion so strange. The F10 M5's 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 produced 552 hp and 501 lb-ft, launching it to 60 mph in as little as 3.7 seconds with launch control. The M5 was the better performer in every department and carried a higher price tag when these particular cars were new, yet collectors are choosing the Japanese sedan regardless. Those buyers know something the road testers never bothered to quantify. The car commanding those prices is the 2016-2020 Lexus GS F, the brand's first and only real shot at the M5. It arrived late to the super-sedan war, conceded the horsepower argument before the first test drive, and left the market quietly when Lexus killed the entire GS line. The enthusiast press respected it, praised its purity, and then recommended the faster Germans anyway. Sales figures reflected that verdict. Just 2,484 GS Fs were built for the US market across the full production run, with 1,418 of those coming in 2016 alone, and annual production never touched 500 cars from 2017 onward. Fewer than 200 units of the final 2020 model year were produced for the American market, making late cars genuinely scarce. Price was a big part of the problem when new. A 2016 GS F carried a starting MSRP of at least $85,000 before options, which was serious money for a sedan that gave up 85 hp to its Bavarian rival. A decade later, that commercial failure has flipped into a rarity floor holding values up. The GS F's 2UR-GSE is the reason the ownership math works, and it starts with how the engine breathes. The naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 was engineered for low weight and high strength, with forged connecting rods and titanium intake and exhaust valves that allow a 7,300-rpm redline, delivering 467 hp and 389 lb-ft of torque. There are no turbochargers to fail, no wastegates to stick, and no intercooler plumbing to leak as the miles pile on. The critical detail is the fueling. The high-pressure D-4S direct injection system also uses port fuel injectors, which allows a high 12.3:1 compression ratio for optimized performance and efficiency. Those port injectors continuously wash fuel over the intake valves, preventing the carbon buildup that chokes direct-injection-only engines as they age — the exact problem that sends aging German turbo motors in for expensive walnut-blasting sessions. The M5 tells the opposite story under the hood. The most severe known issue with the F10's 4.4-liter twin-turbo S63 V8 is rod bearing failure, made worse by BMW's notoriously long oil-change intervals, and the failure list hardly stops there. One of the main reasons the Bavarian car sells so cheaply compared to the Lexus is that it has the potential to bankrupt its owner. The GS F's conventional torque-converter eight-speed automatic completes the durability picture, trading dual-clutch drama for a transmission design with decades of proven service behind it. The financial case extends beyond one auction site, and the clearest data comes from the GS F's mechanical twin. The Lexus RC F coupe shares the same 2UR-GSE V8 and eight-speed automatic, so its ownership data serves as a reliable proxy for the sedan. Its numbers against the equivalent BMW are hard to argue with. Over five years, the BMW M4 loses 44.1 percent of its value while the Lexus RC F loses just 33.6 percent, meaning the Lexus retains 10.5 percentage points more of its value than its direct rival. That makes the RC F the best-performing Lexus of all for resale, retaining 74.9 percent of its value after the first five years. For a luxury performance car, that retention rate is nearly unheard of. Maintenance and repair costs for an RC F amount to just $2,493 over the first five years, according to CarEdge. That beats the luxury coupe segment average by $3,064, and the car carries only a 16.52 percent chance of needing a major repair in that window — 16.43 percent better than its segment peers. Those are Toyota Corolla-grade ownership numbers attached to a 467-hp V8. The GS F lost the 0-60 argument by eight tenths of a second, but it won the 60,000-mile argument by a margin themarket has now priced in at auction. The reader who chose Japanese reliability over German cachet a decade ago is watching the results validate the decision in real time. The car's position in history only strengthens the case. Rear-wheel-drive V8 sedans are dwindling from the market, and the GS F is likely the last of a dying breed, which puts a second floor under values beyond simple rarity. Nobody is building a naturally aspirated, 7,300-rpm luxury sedan again. None of this means shopping blind, because age catches every car eventually. Known GS F checkpoints include wear in the PCV system and the liquid-filled bushings in the lower front control arms, which degrade over time and cause excessive toe-in. That is the entire list of common concerns, and it reads like a single line item next to the M5's catalog of failure modes. That is the real story the auction results are telling. The GS F was never the fastest way to spend $84,440, but it has proven to be the smartest way to own a V8 super-sedan past the warranty period. The market took a decade to do the math, and the math now favors the F badge. Sources: Cars and Bids, Classic, BMW Blog, Car Edge, KBB We want to hear from you. content: When BMW introduced the R12 G/S, it created a curious paradox within its dual-sport lineup. With the flagship R 1300 GS dominating continent-crossing adventure duty and lighter offerings like the F 900 GS or upcoming F 450 GS catering to technical off-road enthusiasts without boxer engines, the retro-focused R12 G/S occupied a unique space. Echoing the lines of the legendary R80 GS, it houses a classic 1,170 cc air/oil-cooled boxer producing 109 hp and 85 lb-ft of torque inside a 505-pound wet package. Yet while it looks the part of an off-road machine with its factory 21-inch front wheel and long-travel suspension, the reality is that few retro-minded buyers ever venture beyond gravel driveways. Ralf Eggl of Woidwerk, a shop out of Bodenmais in the Bavarian Forest that has graced the pages of Bike EXIF several times over the years, recognized this disconnect and saw an opportunity. In his eyes, the platform’s true calling wasn't the trail, but rather a sharp, road-centric canyon carver. Ralf set out to build something minimalist, post-apocalyptic, and undeniably street-oriented without drifting into the supermoto territory. The core of the 1,170 cc engine remained untouched internally, but it received external upgrades to fit its aggressive new purpose. Ralf bolted on Wunderlich cylinder guards and engine protection to safeguard the heads during spirited tarmac riding. To reclaim the visceral mechanical soundtrack muffled by stringent Euro 5 emissions standards, he fitted an Arrow exhaust manifold stripped of its pre-muffler and catalytic converter, pairing it with a steeply angled Hattech silencer at the rear. The result finally allowed the high-compression boxer to roar as intended. The most transformative engineering decision occurred at the chassis level. Reasoning that most R12 G/S owners rarely need an off-road-biased 21-inch front wheel, Ralf swapped it out for a 19-inch rim. This change allowed him to maintain the stock rear wheel while achieving balanced overall geometry reminiscent of the ever-popular R1200GS. He then wrapped the spoked rims in sticky Dunlop Mutant rubber, shedding the dual-sport knobbies in favor of aggressive street and dirt-track traction designed to hook up on mountain twisties. Up front, Ralf stripped away the factory plastic bodywork and rethought the bike's lighting orientation. While he initially considered a Baja-style off-road fairing, he admired the factory full-LED headlight enough to retain it. He fabricated a custom bracket to lower the primary headlight, then mounted an auxiliary Denali fog light diagonally above it to create an asymmetric signature. The handmade bracket doubled as a mounting structure for the OEM instrument cluster. Below the lights, a custom minimalist front fender was shaped from steel, extending the angular lines of the fuel tank, and frame sliders were added to the front forks to signal the motorcycle's intent to go fast and sideways. The rear end underwent an equally thorough simplification. Ralf built a custom tubular steel subframe featuring an integrated grab handle that seamlessly transitions into a custom seat. The custom seat is a mix of Alcantara and glossy synthetic leather to shorten the tail section visually. To echo the vibrant graphic scheme, Ralf added laser-cut arrow stitching backed with bright yellow leather. Because the factory side panels no longer fit the slimmed-down tail section, Ralf enlisted a friend to 3D print custom side covers that hug the airbox tightly, which were then finished in textured Raptor paint. Underneath the subframe, three tiny Kellermann Atto multi-function LED units provide tail and turn lighting, protected from road grime by an acrylic glass panel Although Ralf originally planned to replace the fuel tank with a smaller custom unit, the stark matte black finish on the factory tank highlighted its sharp edges and striking contours so well that he decided to keep it. To make the most of those bold lines, he reached out to Stilbruch-Lack (Style Break Paint), a renowned automotive graphic artist known for a distinct comic and sketch-like visual style. After agreeing on base colors, Ralf gave the artist complete creative freedom. The resulting hand-painted finish gives the motorcycle the uncanny appearance of a 2D concept sketch or AI rendering brought into three-dimensional reality. Built as a direct collaboration with BMW Motorrad dealership Schmidt from Salzburg and BMW Motorrad Austria, the finished Woidwerk machine made its public debut at the Newchurch Summit in Austria. The street-focused build captivated the crowd and even earned the seal of approval from BMW Motorrad CEO Markus Flasch, who took the motorcycle for a test ride around the event’s enduro park. By shifting the focus of the R12 G/S away from dirt heritage and onto asphalt aggression, Ralf Eggl has shown that BMW’s retro boxer makes for an extraordinary road machine. This thing is super cool!! The visuals are off the chart and finally.....a BMW custom that is light-years away from the same same Brat style, flat seat, bland, run of the mill Beemer build.
